newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom drives NZ shares to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Telecom drives NZ shares to higher close.

text.p: * New Zealand shares end higher but off peak
* Rumour driven Telecom drives market up
* Activity in Tranz Rail inflates turnover
253 -7 * NZSE-10 cap index +9.39 at 1,170.66 377 +4 * Volume NZ$132 million. Futures +8 at 1,178
A rumour-driven Telecom shoved New Zealand shares upward at the close on Thursday on turnover heavily inflated by action in Tranz Rail.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 13.68 points higher at 2,338.89 after profit-takers moved in to topple the index from its 2,353.09 peak.

"I think the major factor was that Australia did not follow through at lunchtime. They were down four points at our close and I think that was probably the disappointing part," Nigel Scott at BZW said.
Telecom surged 24 cents, or 3.2 percent, to a new all-time high of NZ$7.70 as well-worn rumours of a capital reduction resurfaced. The stock later eased to close at NZ$7.62.
Telecom declined comment but a spokesman noted the share price had often run up ahead of its result in the past. Telecom reports its first half result next Thursday.

Telecom has a target to keep within a 40-45 percent ratio of net debt to net debt plus equity and was at the bottom end of the range at the end of the first quarter, suggesting it has room to be more aggressively leveraged or to repay capital.
Turnover, worth NZ$132 was heavily influenced by trade in Tranz Rail, with 10.2 million shares, worth NZ$77.3 million, changing hands and the stock ending unchanged at NZ$8.00.
Brokers said U.S. investor Berkshire Partners had sold five million of its 21.9 million shares in New Zealand's Tranz Rail Holdings Ltd at NZ$7.50 per share.
The shares were on-sold to local institutions at NZ$7.60 per share. Tranz Rail's share price has risen strongly from NZ$6.80 on October 9 to a closing high of $8.05 on Tuesday.
